basis: Capacity is planned in missing product rules, not requirements: about 30 per 2-day release. Basis: 53 requirements reached complete in the 14 days to 2026-11-27, at about 3.9 delivered rules each (the verification's mean), so about 15 rules a day. It is recalibrated after each release from the product rules actually delivered. Rules are counted from the 2026-11-27 rule-by-rule verification (req-verify-1127 batches 1-7) against origin/main 9a5d7e81ed; REQ-2196 counts 7 (seven source types) and REQ-2018 counts 10 (ten native-query sources). Coverage-only gaps are not features and are not planned. 513 and 514 list what their code ships: a requirement belongs to the first release whose branch (tag v0.1.0-alpha.512, origin/release/v0.1.0-alpha.513, origin/main for 514) holds every test named for its delivered rules, plus the requirements v1 recorded as completed in that window; requirements whose delivered tests were already at 512 are in the appendix. From 515: the 78 split requirements (REQ-2283..REQ-2360) and the not-started requirements, ordered in-progress first, then MUST, SHOULD, MAY, then remaining work of shipped features and correctness before new surface (demos last within a priority), dependencies first. 138 requirements, 286 product rules.

features.benefit: DBeaver, Metabase, Grafana and psql browse Provisa schemas the same way they browse PostgreSQL, tested against captured real tool traffic.

features.feature: Ephemeral session objects in every language
features.benefit: Users create temporary nodes, rows and graphs in a session without writing to sources, for what-if analysis.
API and native-query tables take typed parameters, so a caller can read an endpoint like /orders/{id} as a table without custom code.

features.feature: VS Code extension for code sources
features.benefit: Developers see which functions Provisa will serve, with inferred columns, and test edits live from their editor before registering anything.
Data engineers read a governed table as a Spark DataFrame, with row rules and masks applied before data leaves Provisa.
Inferred class memberships from an ontology become queryable, so rule-derived categories need no hand-maintained tables.
An org can publish data to the open web from its own subdomain with no login, served only through a read-only public role.
One column can show cleartext to some roles and different masks to others, in a visible precedence order an auditor can check.

features.feature: PII tag by meaning, including future columns
features.benefit: Tagging a business term as PII covers every column with that meaning, including columns added later, so new data is not left unprotected.

features.feature: Per-person entitlements on coarse roles (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2348)
features.benefit: The identity provider grants a person specific tables and columns as attributes, so roles stay few instead of one role per person.

features.feature: Firebase sign-in creates the user profile
features.benefit: Users who sign in with Google or email links get an account on first login without a separate password to manage.

features.feature: One naming authority for client-facing names
features.benefit: Every client sees the same governed names on SQL, GraphQL and Cypher, and physical column names never leak to users.
Glossary, ontology, metrics, tags, classification and documents sit under one menu, so stewards find the context layer in one place.

features.feature: One-script Linux host install with Trino
features.benefit: An operator installs Provisa with a Trino engine on an existing Linux VM or server with one command, without Kubernetes.
Native-query and parameterized tables have predictable caching, so users know when they see live data and when a kept copy.

features.feature: The model store (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2308)
features.benefit: Sources, tables, roles, rules and products are held in one versioned store per org, the base for environments, sync and git projection.

features.feature: Catalogs admin panel (publish and read) (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2331)
features.benefit: Each catalog connection is set up once and used both to publish and to read metadata.

features.feature: Names across the whole data estate
features.benefit: Every admitted object, export and grounded column term gets a checked, clash-free name, and only the worker that changed the model rewrites the names, so names stay consistent as the model grows.
SQL clients over the PostgreSQL protocol get large results many times faster (measured 14x text, 40x binary) with every PostgreSQL type supported.
Money and decimal columns keep their exact digits on every engine and protocol, so financial figures never round differently by client.

features.feature: Relate tables right after registering them
features.benefit: Source setup ends with proposed relationships for the new tables, so a first query can join them minutes after connecting.
The ERD, lane diagram and ontology graph look and behave alike, so users read every diagram the same way.
The assistant fills forms and presses buttons while the user watches, so new users learn the product by seeing each step done.

features.feature: Docker image builds its own UI
features.benefit: Every published image carries the UI built from the same commit, so the console always matches the server.

features.feature: Wrapper-catalog services as brands (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2306)
features.benefit: Stripe, OpenMetadata and DataHub connect as brands over the OpenAPI source, with no API spec to find.

features.feature: Spark connector in Sources (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2350)
features.benefit: Teams connect a Spark cluster as a source from the UI with the cluster as structured fields, without writing glue code.

features.feature: Discovered code-source tables and live API sources (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2360)
features.benefit: A code source can generate its own tables and relationships at discovery, and OpenAPI and GraphQL sources run as built-in code sources.

features.feature: Data product access requests (delivered rules; the rest is REQ-2340)
features.benefit: A user who can see a product but not read it asks its owner in one step, and the grant is recorded instead of handled by email.

features.feature: Column rules by tag or classification
features.benefit: One rule hides or masks every column carrying a tag such as PII, wherever it appears, instead of maintaining rules column by column.
Masked JSON columns return realistic fake objects with the right shape, so test and demo environments work without real personal data.

notes: Provisa's GitHub organization becomes simpleishard-llc with this release: the repository, release assets and container images (ghcr.io/simpleishard-llc) move there (maintainer 2026-11-27).

features.benefit: Approvers get an email with approve and deny links when a creation request is raised, so requests do not sit unseen.

features.feature: Generated break-glass password with forced rotation
features.benefit: The emergency admin account cannot be used from a leaked config file or a reused password.
An installation can never lock itself out of platform administration.
Auditors can see who deleted an org and when, after its data is gone.

features.feature: High availability as published recovery time
features.benefit: Every tier gets a stated recovery time in minutes, so buyers can plan around it without paying for an HA upgrade.
Clients on pgwire, Bolt, gRPC or MCP are load-balanced across every node of a cluster.
Kubernetes operators get certificates issued and renewed automatically instead of managing TLS Secrets by hand.
Higher tiers get more concurrency and memory on shared Trino, so paying tenants are not throttled like free ones.

features.feature: Schema-only boot replicas on every engine
features.benefit: Restarts are fast and never re-copy source data.

features.feature: Edit conflicts and one reconcile path
features.benefit: Two admins can no longer silently overwrite each other's model edits.

features.feature: URI reserved words and rename aliases
features.benefit: Catalogs that stored an object's old address still find it after a rename.

features.feature: OneLake catalog target; user descriptions kept
features.benefit: Microsoft Fabric shops publish to OneLake, and no catalog path overwrites descriptions people wrote.

features.feature: Bind environment sources from the CLI
features.benefit: Environment setup is scriptable in CI without the UI.
Admins see at a glance which environments still need data bindings.
Every model change is versioned and synced the same way, whatever was edited.
No engine statement runs without a verified authorization, closing the last ungoverned paths.
Company-wide metrics are defined once and visible to every domain.

features.feature: One naming authority end to end
features.benefit: Names suggested before saving and names shown after saving come from one place, so a table or relationship is called the same thing in the UI, the API and every query language.
JSON queries give the same answer on every engine, and type drift is caught instead of returning wrong data.
inet, money and range columns are always readable on every engine.
Buyers see where each PostgreSQL equivalence was verified and which source-specific hints apply.

features.feature: Shared named types on every surface
features.benefit: Nested objects and enums appear as named, reused types in GraphQL and gRPC, so generated client code stays small and stable.

features.feature: Generated files always in the org folder
features.benefit: One org's generated code and data never land where another org's process can read them.
Each metric has an accountable owner, and only they or an org admin change it.
Alation customers get Provisa's model in their catalog like the other supported catalogs.

features.feature: Contract type check and alias names
features.benefit: Consumers are warned when a source breaks a data contract, and never see physical column names.

features.feature: Role and column requests; suggestion outcomes
features.benefit: Buyers ask for the role and columns they need in one form and see what was decided.
Enterprise prospects reach sales from the site without needing a mail client.
Materialized-view refreshes cannot slow interactive queries.

features.feature: Opt out of view answers per request
features.benefit: An analyst who needs the live base-table answer bypasses pre-aggregated views for one query without changing the model.
A small Helm install runs Trino in one pod, and larger ones add workers when queries queue, not only when CPU is busy.

features.feature: Mandatory config download on org deletion
features.benefit: No org is deleted without a restorable copy of its configuration.

features.feature: Ops trend, usage and freshness reports
features.benefit: Operators see trends, resource use and data freshness in built-in reports instead of ad-hoc log queries.
Operators monitor Provisa in their existing Prometheus and OpenTelemetry stack.
A wrong Helm value fails at install with a clear message instead of a broken deployment.
Windows users on WSL2 reach the UI from their Windows browser without manual port setup.
Analysts join tag assignments with data in SQL and see only what their role may see.
Snowflake consumers see which business domain owns a listed product.

features.feature: Crawl-scope fields in the source form
features.benefit: Admins limit what an HTTP crawl follows from the UI instead of editing config.

features.feature: Wikidata endpoints, Atlassian brands, Wikidata grounding
features.benefit: Atlassian Cloud or Data Center and custom Wikidata endpoints connect by brand, and terms can point to shared Wikidata meanings.

features.feature: Scalar OpenAPI and gRPC operations as functions
features.benefit: Single-value API calls are used in queries as functions, the same as GraphQL scalars.

features.feature: Google Sheets OAuth, per-sheet tables, refresh
features.benefit: Each tab of a spreadsheet becomes its own table under the user's own Google sign-in.
Protobuf Kafka topics are queryable, and schema changes are caught before they break readers.
Admins hide unwanted API endpoints from the UI without editing config.

features.feature: Cached rewrite on Flight SQL, Cypher and Bolt
features.benefit: Repeated queries over Flight SQL, Cypher and Bolt return faster.
Graph tools see the same labels whether they connect over Bolt or HTTP.
Users cannot remove saved settings with one accidental click.

features.feature: Deprecate metrics, roles and row rules
features.benefit: Teams retire any model object with a warning period, not only tables and columns.
Trial assistant use has a hard, visible spending cap.
Self-hosted Jira shops query issues the same way Cloud users do.

features.feature: Registered remote hosts for code sources
features.benefit: Code sources run on the customer's own machines, close to their data.
Organizations detect their own identifiers, such as employee ids, the way built-in kinds are detected.

features.feature: Teradata, Db2, Vertica, Netezza, Informix, Sybase, Spanner sources
features.benefit: Enterprises with legacy warehouses query them directly beside modern sources.

features.feature: Catalog approvers and Alation data products
features.benefit: Catalog users request access from the right approvers, and Alation shops see products too.

features.feature: Catalog pick list, refresh and lock
features.benefit: Stewards reuse descriptions already written in their catalog and keep one source of truth.

features.feature: Ontology graph export; focus carried to queries
features.benefit: Teams take the governed ontology into other RDF tools and keep their focus when moving to a query.
Large ontology graphs open in one request.
Ontology counts are per real-world entity, and Purview shows each term's role.
Citations to spreadsheets stay correct as the sheet changes.
Terms found in a document turn into model relationships in one step.

features.feature: Policy tags with gates and why-not answers
features.benefit: Every refusal explains which policy caused it, and policy tags enforce exports and promotion without custom code.

features.feature: Entitlements tab, why-not trace, preview as
features.benefit: Admins see and test exactly what a person can reach without signing in as them.

features.feature: Code connector catalog, setup fields and Flight
features.benefit: Organizations build full connectors in code, with typed setup forms and fast Arrow reads.
Prospects see Spark data governed and joined with other sources end to end.

features.feature: One serving path for OpenAPI and GraphQL
features.benefit: API sources behave identically however they were added, with one code path to fix and secure.
dbt test results show up as Provisa data quality, with no second test framework.
Teams adopt new versions of standard ontologies like FIBO deliberately, seeing what changed.

features.feature: Sync schedules, webhooks and full take-from-catalog
features.benefit: Catalog and Provisa stay in step on a schedule, with differences decided by people or the customer's own workflow.
Undoing a removal keeps history and links, and broken references are found, not discovered by users.

features.feature: Identical remote-schema handling for all adapters
features.benefit: GraphQL, gRPC and OpenAPI sources classify and register operations the same way, so behavior is predictable across source types.
Bulleted and numbered lists on web pages become tables, widening what a file source can read.
Admins see why no tables were discovered instead of an empty list.
The Calcite connector runtime loads once and is shared by every pgwire server, cutting memory and start time per source.
Sources reached through Calcite report column sizes and types like Provisa's own server, so SQL tools display them correctly.

features.feature: Calcite dialect fixes at the source
features.benefit: SQL sent to JDBC sources is fixed in the Calcite dialect, so every source on that dialect benefits.

features.feature: Production Db2, Trino, Vertica and Firebolt dialects
features.benefit: These four databases get correct pushed-down SQL, so queries against them return right answers.
An org publishing a data portal shows its own brand on the glossary and Explore pages it exposes.

features.feature: One endpoint for valid join paths
features.benefit: Agents and the join guard get the same list of valid paths between two tables, so AI-generated joins follow approved relationships.
AI-written descriptions never read or change tables outside the domains a steward is working in.

features.feature: Citations agents can hand over intact
features.benefit: Agent answers carry a citation of the governed path and its trust, so a person can verify where an answer came from.

features.feature: Customer 360 demo: match quality and a second question
features.benefit: Prospects see entity-resolution quality measured, not asserted.

features.feature: OSV data in the vulnerabilities demo
features.benefit: The demo answers exposure questions with real public vulnerability data.

features.feature: Rate and cost caps on public endpoints
features.benefit: Published anonymous endpoints have the tightest limits, so a public data portal cannot run up engine costs or be abused.

features.feature: One consequences gate on every model save
features.benefit: Every create, update or delete from UI, API, config load or agent is checked the same way before it reaches the model.

features.feature: Base and derived relations without a sentinel source
features.benefit: Views and metrics show their real lineage instead of a placeholder source, so provenance reads correctly.

features.feature: Buyer view of a data product
features.benefit: A user who cannot yet read a product sees what it offers and how to request it, which turns the catalog into a self-serve storefront.
SQL Server, Oracle, ClickHouse, Redshift, Exasol and others are reached through a dedicated JDBC pack where the engines' own connectors fall short.

features.feature: Spark Connect catalog as a source
features.benefit: Provisa reads a Spark cluster's databases and tables through Spark Connect, so lakehouse tables join with other sources in one query.

features.feature: Approve or deny org join requests
features.benefit: Org admins approve people who ask to join, so teams onboard colleagues without a support ticket.

features.feature: Role members from SCIM, LDAP, Graph and Google
features.benefit: Reviews and reports see who actually holds a role, whatever system manages membership.
Environments are enabled by license feature rather than product name, so edition upgrades turn them on without a reinstall.
Operators send support a log file with secrets and personal data removed.
Graph traversals over a materialized relationship read a prebuilt edge index, speeding large-graph queries.

features.feature: Volatile tables never served from copies
features.benefit: Tables marked volatile always read live, so time-critical data is never stale.
Roles, rules and masks carry review schedules with recorded sign-off, which auditors ask for.
Users ask for a table or column they found, and the request becomes a reviewed grant.
Admins see exactly what a set of roles and session values can read and why, answering access questions in seconds.
A client written for SQL Server or another database connects without rewriting its SQL.

features.feature: Text search as an API query pattern
features.benefit: Tables offer stemmed text search from their API tab with no search engine to set up.
Tags appear as nodes linked to the tables and columns they mark, so graph queries can traverse governance.
Commands are called from SQL and Cypher with parameters and column values, so queries stay parameterised.
SQL users and BI tools find tables regardless of letter case.
Engines can run queries as the requesting user, so engine-side audit logs name the real person.

features.feature: Published data over pgwire and Bolt
features.benefit: Published open data is readable from SQL clients and graph tools without a login, not only over HTTP.

features.feature: Production access requests built on branches
features.benefit: Production users get access through a reviewed, time-limited request instead of new roles.

features.feature: Assistant tests columns against policy sections
features.benefit: Stewards get a fast, governed first check of policy compliance without the assistant making legal claims.

features.feature: OpenLineage import of sources and tables
features.benefit: Teams that already emit OpenLineage bootstrap their Provisa model from it instead of registering tables by hand.

features.feature: Collibra, Alation, Atlan, OneLake and Dataplex as sources
features.benefit: Governance teams query catalog metadata beside live data to find where catalog and enforcement disagree.
Source introspection through each engine returns complete table lists.

features.feature: Copy or move a table to another source
features.benefit: A table is copied under governance to another source, for migrations or offloading.
The model exports to dbt semantic and Cube formats, so existing BI layers reuse it.

features.feature: Refer creation requests to another domain
features.benefit: Stewards hand a request to the right domain with a note instead of rejecting it.
Process terms such as "close of day" point to the commands that carry them out.
Metrics from a PromQL query join business data in SQL, so operations and business numbers sit in one report.
A unary gRPC call becomes a parameterized table.
Hybrid dense and sparse vector search with fusion is available as a table.
SAP and Microsoft OData services connect from a service URL with no handwritten spec.

features.feature: Drivers for sources, engines and secrets
features.benefit: Every built-in implementation is a driver, so partners extend Provisa the same way.
Users save a named query and return to it, without creating a shared view.
Each source type's facts live in one descriptor, so adding a source type touches one place.
Delta, Iceberg and Hudi tables on Spark answer as-of queries, so audits and restatements read past versions directly.
Inserts, updates and deletes on Delta and Iceberg tables are served as change data for downstream sync.
Maintenance such as compaction and snapshot expiry runs as governed commands from Provisa.

features.feature: OneDrive and Google Drive file crawling
features.benefit: Hosted and server installs read files straight from OneDrive and Google Drive, with no desktop sync client.
Teams connect common SaaS tools by picking a brand and signing in, with no API spec to find.

features.feature: Custom Great Expectations checks as commands
features.benefit: Teams extend quality checks with their own Python functions through the same governed command surface.
Lineage held in Marquez is queryable through its public API.
Unity Catalog functions and MLflow models are offered as governed functions.
Records that refer to the same customer or product across sources are linked in one shared map, so cross-source questions return one answer per entity.
Notes and documents link to the products and tables they mention, so unstructured text joins structured data.
Shows KYC ownership chains with OWL transitive control reasoning.
Shows products offered to an organisation's own people with existing primitives.
Shows an analyst seeing why a column is masked, requesting it, and getting a governed grant.
Shows a dbt project governed by role with lineage, unchanged.
Shows insured value inside this week's wildfire perimeter and which policyholders to call first.
An org copies an environment with bindings, secrets and users when it wants the control plane as it stands.
A developer works against a non-prod environment's model on their own machine.

features.feature: SPARQL Update to curation and commands
features.benefit: RDF tools curate the ontology and run commands under the same rights as the UI.
Snowflake users see governed views organized by domain in a clean database.
